extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers; journalists and policymakers interested in Cold War/foreign affairs
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and interpretive coverage of major foreign‑policy events (here: a Kremlin purge), combining factual dispatches, reactions from other countries, analysis of implications, and biographical sketches of key figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use competent sources
rubrics_metrics.description: "COMPETENT SOURCES, SAID, HOWEVER, REPERCUSSIONS OUTSIDE THE SOVIET ..." (page uses the phrase 'competent sources').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute analysis and predictions to named or described reliable sources; when discussing likely repercussions or motives, qualify assertions by noting they come from "competent sources" or similar attribution rather than presenting speculation as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include international reactions and editorials
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple paragraphs cite foreign newspapers and commentaries (e.g., ZYCIE WARSZAWY: 'EVENTS IN MOSC... FILL US WITH OPTIMISM.'; British papers' editorials; Yugoslav and Italian reactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather and report reactions from a range of international and regional press outlets and official agencies to show how the event is perceived abroad; use direct quotes from editorials where salient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain significance beyond borders
rubrics_metrics.description: Text explicitly states the ouster 'IS AN ACHIEVEMENT EXTENDING IN ITS IMPORTANCE FAR BEYOND THE FRONTIERS OF THE USSR.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize events in terms of regional and global consequences — e.g., likely effects on Eastern Europe, NATO, Sino‑Soviet relations — rather than treating them as purely domestic developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical background and context
rubrics_metrics.description: References to Stalin's death, the 20th Party Congress, the Hungarian uprising, prior purges, and past policy disputes (e.g., Malenkov's earlier firing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed current developments in concise historical narrative linking them to prior events and policy trends so readers can assess continuity and change; cite relevant past incidents and congresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include on‑the‑ground observations and public sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of street reactions and direct quotes from ordinary citizens: 'I don't believe it's true,' 'They had it coming,' noting tourists and crowds at the Lenin‑Stalin mausoleum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment official and analytical material with eyewitness reportage and vox populi quotations to convey public mood and social atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report official communiqués and party statements verbatim or summarized
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of the Central Committee resolution, denunciations of the expelled group, and official language accusing them of 'deviationism and collusion to split up' the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present key wording from government/party communiqués (or accurate summaries) so readers can see the official rationale and charges; note collective/unanimous decisions when reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide biographical sketches of new appointees
rubrics_metrics.description: Section titled 'HERE ARE BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCHES IN BRIEF ON THE NINE NEW FULL MEMBERS...' with career summaries for each new Presidium member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When leadership changes occur, include concise bios (age, career path, prior posts, political alignment) for replacements to clarify who now holds power and their backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate interpretive/analytical pieces from straight dispatches
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels such as 'UNDATED SOVIET INTERPRETIVE' and use of analyst commentary (e.g., 'SOVIET INTERPRETIVE' and 'ANALYSTS HERE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly mark analysis or interpretive articles and distinguish them from news dispatches; make explicit when content is the reporter's or analysts' interpretation rather than a factual dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present multiple viewpoints (Western, Soviet, Chinese, satellite states)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage includes Western officials' views, Soviet radio statements, Peiping/Chinese broadcasts, and reactions from Poland, Yugoslavia, East Germany, Romania, Hungary, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the story by including perspectives from different geopolitical actors and local/regional governments to reflect contested interpretations and diplomatic repercussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze policy and strategic implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of how the purge affects 'peaceful coexistence', NATO, Sino‑Soviet relations, the likelihood of Khrushchev becoming 'strong man' or dictator, and consequences for disarmament talks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to reporting facts, assess likely policy outcomes and strategic effects (e.g., on alliances, arms talks), making clear the basis for such assessments (sources, expert opinion, historical parallels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include dateline, byline, and wire service attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple stories include datelines and bylines (e.g., 'BY JOHN RODERICK', 'LONDON, JULY 4 (AP)', 'BY ROY ESSOYAN (AP)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear datelines, bylines, and news‑agency credits to identify origin, time, and authorship of dispatches; this establishes provenance and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report personnel changes and exact positions affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific reporting that 'MOLOTOV, MALENKOV AND KAGANOVICH HAD BEEN REMOVED FROM THEIR GOVERNMENT POSITIONS' and identification of demotions and appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List who was removed, demoted, or promoted and the precise offices affected (Presidium, government posts, party secretariats) to provide an accurate account of the shift in formal power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotations from named officials to substantiate claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations attributed to figures such as Deputy Premier Anastas Mikoyan, Premier Nehru, Harold E. Stassen, and others are used throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support reporting and analysis with direct quotes from named officials and diplomats; attribute clearly and preserve quote fidelity to strengthen credibility.
